problem: Existing VLN models mostly use RGB features only, and naively adding a depth stream gives only marginal improvement even though real robots have depth sensors.
motivation: Robots have depth sensors, so exploiting RGB-D should help navigation. Simply adding a depth stream is not effective, so a better way to use geometric and semantic information from RGB-D is needed, ideally without large-scale vision-language transformer pretraining.
key_idea: Build semantic map observations from RGB-D input and encode them with a vision-pretrained CNN and a scene query attention network that learns by answering queries about the semantic content of specific scene regions.
insight: Only the abstract was available. It claims that semantic-map encoding pretrained through query answering makes depth useful in a simple model, giving more than 10% SR gain over a baseline. Ablation details are not available.
method: Semantic map observation: builds a semantic map from RGB-D input as the model's visual input.
CNN map encoder: encodes the semantic map, with vision pretraining.
Scene query attention network: pretrained by answering queries about semantic information of specific scene regions.
Speaker-Follower training: combined with the method for extra gains (data augmentation).

setting.backbone: CNN semantic-map encoder + scene query attention network + simple VLN follower (trained, no large-scale VL transformer pretraining)
setting.training_data: R2R with vision-pretraining on semantic query answering; Speaker-Follower augmentation in one variant (scale not stated in abstract)

numbers.backbone: CNN semantic map encoder + scene query attention network
numbers.evidence: abstract: 'it achieves a success rate of 58 % on the test set for the R2R dataset in single-run setting'

numbers_note: abstract only; the full tables were not available, and the abstract's 'test set' is presumed to be the R2R test-unseen split.
results: Over 10% SR improvement over a baseline model, and 58% SR on R2R test in single-run with Speaker-Follower training. It outperforms the previous RGB-D method and most RGB-only models that do not use large-scale VL transformer pretraining.
limitations: Does not compete with large-scale vision-language pretrained transformers (implied by the comparison scope)
Depends on semantic map construction from RGB-D, with evaluation only in simulation as far as the abstract shows
